names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 februarie, «Sfânta Muceniță Fotini Samarineanca».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Φεβρουαρίου, «Αγία Φωτεινή η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Σαμαρείτιδα», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's second heading for the Julian 20 March on pravoslavno.rs, „Света мученица Фотина.“, with Света left off, which is not a rank, and with the rank word мученица left off. The heading gives no epithet — the Samaritan woman is the body's first clause and not part of the name — so the bare forename is what the source gives. Note the spelling: the Prologue has Фотина where the Greek form already in this folder is Φωτεινή.

The heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name page 2742, «Мученица Фотина (Светлана) Самаряныня, Римская», with the rank word left off. The day's own line declines it and drops the city, «Мц. Фотины (Светланы) самаряныни». The bracketed «Светлана» is the calendar's own and is part of what it prints, as the brackets of a surname are elsewhere in this wave.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 20 марта ст. ст. — «Мц. Фотины (Светланы) самаряныни, ее сыновей мчч. Виктора, нареченного Фотином, и Иосии; мцц. Анатолии, Фото, Фотиды, Параскевы, Кириакии, Домнины и мч. Севастиана (ок. 66).»

attestations.note: The calendar prints the whole company of eleven on one line and closes it «(ок. 66)», which is the only year it gives any of them; its life repeats the folder's existing bounds word for word — «Во времена императора Нерона (54 - 68)» — so the dates are left as they stand and the «ок. 66» is recorded here rather than chosen. The russian form adds «Светлана», the Russian rendering of her name that the calendar prints in brackets beside it. The reading behind the line adds what this folder did not hold: that she lived at Carthage with her younger son and preached there, that her elder son was a commander in the Roman armies, that the hands of the confessors were broken on an anvil and hers alone were left whole, that the skin was flayed from her and she was thrown into a well, drawn out, kept twenty days in prison, and thrown back into it to die. One arrival comes off this line, the daughter of Nero set to guard her in the palace and converted by her, and a `related` row is added for her. The day page prints no hymn for this company. The name page, 2742, lists this day and no other; the Romanian and Greek rows keep her on 26 February and the Serbian already on this same Julian 20 March.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 februarie — «Sfânta Muceniță Fotini Samarineanca»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Αγία Φωτεινή η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Σαμαρείτιδα»
Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 02.04.2026 (20. март ст. ст.) — „Света мученица Фотина.“

attestations.note: The day's second and last entry, and plainly this woman: the Samaritan who spoke with the Lord at Jacob's well by Shechem, whom the entry places by the Gospel reference itself (Јн 4, 1-42), and who died in the reign of Nero, which is the interval this folder already holds. The Prologue keeps her on the Julian 20 March, where the Romanian and the Greek keep her on 26 February; the churches differ and nothing here moves either. **The row is hers alone.** The body names her two sons and her five sisters, and says that after the imprisonment they all suffered for Christ — but the heading names only Фотина, with no „и други“ to reach them, and the seven are recorded in this note and in the life rather than given rows, as the senator Asterius was on the Julian 17 March. All seven are folders this corpus already holds on the Greek and Romanian 26 February, and all seven are already `related` to this folder in both directions. One of the seven is a name question: the Prologue calls the first son **Виктор** where the Greek calendar calls him Φωτεινός and this corpus keeps him as `photinos-son-of-photini`. Recorded, not resolved, and no Serbian form was stored on his folder. Nero's daughter Домнина, whom the entry has converted by Photina in prison, was not read as any of the corpus's Domninas and takes nothing. The stored form is the bare forename — Света мученица is the rank and the heading carries no Самарјанка — and no other folder in the corpus holds a Serbian Фотина. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

death.note: saint.gr gives no year and prints the reign: «Εκεί έλαβε και μαρτυρικό θάνατο από τον αυτοκράτορα Νέρωνα (54 - 68), όταν αυτός έμαθε ότι η Αγία Φωτεινή έκανε Χριστιανές τη θυγατέρα του Δομνίνα και μερικές δούλες της.»

hymns.text: Τὴν πηγὴν δεξαμενὴ τῆς σοφίας καὶ χάριτος, ἐκ χειλέων Κυρίου Φωτεινὴ Ἰσαπόστολε, νομίμως ἠγωνίσω πανοικεῖ, καὶ νέμεις φωτισμὸν παρὰ Θεοῦ, τοὶς προστρέχουσι τὴ σκέπη σου τὴ σεπτή, καὶ εὐλαβῶς βοώσί σου. Δόξα τῷ δεδωκότι σοι ἰσχύν, δόξα τῷ σὲ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ χορηγούντι διὰ σοῦ, χάριν ἠμὶν καὶ ἔλεος.

source.text: Ορθόδοξος Συναξαριστής (saint.gr) — Αγία Φωτεινή η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Σαμαρείτιδα, Λειτουργικά κείμενα: Ἀπολυτίκιον

english.text: Having received from the Lord's own lips the spring of wisdom and of grace, Photini equal to the apostles, you contended lawfully with your whole household, and you dispense enlightenment from God to those who run to your honoured shelter and reverently cry to you: glory to him who gave you strength, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who through you furnishes grace and mercy to us.

hymns.text: Φωτεινὴν καὶ Φωτίδα καὶ Φωτῶ ἀνυμνήσωμεν, σὺν Ἀνατολὴ Φωτεινὸν τὲ Ἰωσὴν θείοις ἄσμασιν, ὁμοὺ Κυριακὴν Παρασκευήν, τοὺς Μάρτυρας Χριστοῦ περιφανεῖς· θείαν χάριν γὰρ αἰτοῦνται καὶ φωτισμόν, τοὶς πίστει ἀνακράζουσι· δόξα τῷ ἐνισχύσαντι ὑμᾶς, δόξα τῷ στεφανώσαντι, δόξα τῷ ἐνεργούντι δι' ὑμῶν πάσιν ἰάματα.

source.text: Ορθόδοξος Συναξαριστής (saint.gr) — Αγία Φωτεινή η Μεγαλομάρτυς η Σαμαρείτιδα, Λειτουργικά κείμενα: Έτερον Ἀπολυτίκιον. It is the whole company's apolytikion, printed under her name and naming her first.

english.text: Let us hymn Photini and Photis and Photo, with Anatole and Photinos and Joses, in divine songs, and Kyriake and Paraskeve together, the illustrious martyrs of Christ; for they ask divine grace and enlightenment for those who cry out to them in faith: glory to him who strengthened you, glory to him who crowned you, glory to him who works healings for all through you.
